## Tidying and Having Technically Correct Data from the PlaneCrash Info Site

```{r crashes}
year = 2025

crash_url = paste0('https://www.planecrashinfo.com/', year, '/', year, '.htm')

# the encoding came from chatisa as shown in class 12
crash_page <- rvest::read_html(crash_url, encoding = "ISO-8859-1")

crash_page |> 
  # selector from inspector (kept the last three parts of the selector)
  # note the output (we also dropped :nth-child(8) in tr since we want all rows)
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(1) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> date_col

crash_page |> 
  # repeat for location_operator
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(2) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> location_operator

crash_page |> 
  # repeat for aircraft_reg
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> aircraft_reg

crash_page |> 
  # repeat for fatalities
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(4) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> fatalities

# note that the number elements in the four vectors are not equal
df = data.frame(
  date_col = date_col, 
  # -1 drops the first row that had the col header
  location_operator = location_operator[-1],
  aircraft_reg = aircraft_reg[-1],
  fatalities = fatalities[-1]
)

# make this tidy

df |> 
  tidyr::separate(col = location_operator, into = c("location", "operator"), sep = "\n") |> 
  tidyr::separate(col = aircraft_reg, into = c("aircraft", "registeration"), sep = "\n") |> 
  tidyr::separate(col = fatalities, into = c("air_fatalities", "num_pass", "ground_fatalities")) -> tidy_df
```
